locator.text: Display 125.3, p. 125, in the proof of Corollary 10.6

evidence: paper: \widetilde{u}(x,t) = \lambda u(\lambda x, \lambda^{2}(t-t_{0})), \qquad \widetilde{p}(x,t) = \lambda^{2} p(\lambda x, \lambda^{2}(t-t_{0})), \qquad \widetilde{f}(x,t) = \lambda^{3} f(\lambda x, \lambda^{2}(t-t_{0})).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Term by term the amplitudes agree (λ, λ², λ³ ↔ l, l^2, l^3) and the spatial dilation agrees (λx ↔ l • x); Lean puts time first in the pair. The time change is written differently but is the same affine map: the paper fixes t₀ = 1 − λ⁻² one line above the display, and λ²(t − t₀) = λ²t − λ² + 1 = λ²(t−1)+1 = clock l t, so the rewriting is this one-line identity. Lean additionally composes u and p with zeroBefore, which truncates to zero exactly where clock l t < 0, i.e. t < t₀; on the display's stated range t ≥ t₀ it is inert, and it encodes the paper's next sentence ("We extend all three by zero for t < t₀"). force applies no zeroBefore, but compressedCandidate carries hc.force_support : CompactPositiveTimeSupport f (tsupport f ⊆ Ioi 0 × univ), so f vanishes at nonpositive times and force l f already vanishes for t ≤ t₀ without the wrapper.
